objective: Persist and enforce stable real-outcome identity for scored Quest v2 creation so retries, renamed quests, and new quest instance IDs cannot accidentally earn progression twice for the same outcome/cadence.

roles_before.artifact: quest_id uniquely identifies a quest instance.
system-quest-difficulty:v1 requires an outcome_key and existing_outcome_keys for duplicate detection, but Quest v2 creation does not persist that key.
system-quest-reward:v1 constrains amounts and progression.award constrains one award per completion basis.
Existing Quest v1/v2 events and unscored quests remain readable and actionable.
system_events is append-only and Neon is the sole mutable owner of derived RPG state.
Production schema/player mutation requires separate exact authorization; candidate work must not change production.
Current main remains exact rollback provenance.

role_dispositions.destination: quest_id remains the unique quest-instance identity.

Scored Quest v2 creation persists normalized outcome_key and optional outcome_cadence in the quest.created payload, and the write gate rejects duplicate scored outcome identity inside the same declared cadence.
Existing reward calibration, verified completion, atomic quest.resolve, and one-award-per-completion rules remain unchanged.
Historical events without outcome_key remain valid; unscored/legacy quest creation remains supported.
No updates/deletes or second state owner; only new validated quest.created payload fields/indexing logic are added.
Candidate branch and CI only. No production schema/data/main promotion until exact authorization and full verification.
Base SHA 882bcf090de27b7608733bb925b674ec12494974 remains the exact rollback point.

capability_probes.assertion: Existing unscored and legacy quest.create behavior remains accepted.
A second scored Quest v2 with a different quest_id but the same normalized outcome_key and cadence is rejected before rewardable state is created.
A retry of an expired unrewarded outcome can be represented explicitly without minting a second reward identity; policy distinguishes attempt identity from reward outcome identity.
quest.resolve atomic completion/reward tests still pass unchanged.
The exact base SHA preserves the pre-outcome-key runtime and all historical player data remains readable.

tests.expected: Quest v2 scored creation persists normalized outcome identity and duplicate scored outcome/cadence is rejected.
PostgreSQL action gate enforces the same outcome identity semantics.
